items.title: John Beal interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 18, 2024
items.q: like Mingus, you know the way he’d rehearse a band, they didn’t have music

ctx.x: patterns etcetera. They’re not concerned with that, they’re concerned with if it sounds good then it is good.

Yeah. I mean I’ll go along with that. Yeah I mean sometimes I’ll play with a younger player that might not know a tune, he goes on his phone and looks it up and he’s playing from his phone. And it’s like I don’t get it, you know. Like for instance, like Mingus, you know the way he’d rehearse a band, they didn’t have music, they’d make up — you know he’d sing the parts or he’d rehearse, he’d develop it without music you know. And you could do that with a small group.

This is almost an aside but I watched an interview with you, I think it was fairly recent, it was another young man there, and somehow this bit about fixed Do and movable Do came up. And I have to say I’d never heard of such a thing until my own daughter brought it up, who is a music teacher, and it was something about Eastman School of Music. And I said, “What are you talking about?”
